claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me: **How many children are you responsible for, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I have one child - my son Alex. I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me start by asking: **How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 19.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know that Alex is 19.

Since Alex is over 16, there are specific rules that apply. Let me ask: **Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's studying for his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. A-levels are approved education, so that's positive for eligibility.

Now I need to understand your living situation: **Do you live with Alex, or does he live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you for clarifying that you live with Alex.

Now I need to check one more important thing: **Are you currently receiving any of the following benefits: Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any of those benefits.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have one final question to complete the assessment:

**What is your individual annual income (before tax)?**

This is important because there's a tax charge on Child Benefit if either you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000 per year. This won't affect your eligibility to receive Child Benefit, but it's important information for you to know.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into that right now - I'm just trying to figure out if I can actually claim it in the first place. Is there anything else you need to know about Alex's situation?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's completely fair! You don't need to worry about the income tax charge question right now - that's something you can look into separately if you decide to claim.

Let me ask just one more thing to make sure I have everything I need:

**Are you the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is someone else also claiming for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, his mum already claims Child Benefit for him. We're separated and he lives with both of us, really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that - this is important information.

Since Alex's mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him, I need to understand the situation a bit better:

**How much time does Alex spend living with you versus living with his mum - roughly what proportion of the time is he at your home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with me full-time now. He used to split his time, but he's been living at my place for the past year or so.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. This is an important change in circumstances.

Since Alex has been living with you full-time for the past year, but his mum is currently receiving Child Benefit for him, I have one more question:

**Has his mum been informed that Alex is now living with you full-time, or has she continued to claim Child Benefit without knowing about this change in living arrangements?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She knows he's living with me. We're in touch about Alex and she's still claiming it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is a key detail.

I now have enough information to assess your eligibility. Let me explain the situation:

According to the Child Benefit rules, only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child. Since Alex's mum is currently claiming Child Benefit for him, and you're asking about claiming as well, here's what applies:

**You would need to agree with his mum about who should claim Child Benefit for Alex.** Since he's living with you full-time, you could potentially be the one to claim. However, this would require:

1. His mum to stop her claim, and
2. You to make a new claim for Alex

The rules state that if you and someone else are responsible for the same child, you must agree between yourselves who will get Child Benefit. If you can't agree, HMRC will decide.

**One final question to complete my assessment: Would you like me to evaluate your eligibility assuming you and his mum have agreed that you should be the one to claim going forward?** Or would you prefer a different scenario for the evaluation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, let's assume we've sorted that out and she's agreed I should claim it since he lives with me now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect, thank you for clarifying that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Great news! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 19 and in approved education (A-levels), so you can claim for him as he's under 20 and still in full-time education
- You live with him full-time, which makes you responsible for him
- You're not receiving any of the benefits that would disqualify you
- His mother has agreed that you should be the claimant

**What you need to do next:**
1. Make sure his mother stops her Child Benefit claim for Alex
2. Contact HMRC to make a new claim for Child Benefit for Alex yourself

The key thing to remember is that only one person can claim Child Benefit per child, so it's important that his mother officially stops her claim before you start yours to avoid any complications with HMRC.
